questions.question: How do the red algae reproduce vegetatively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Fragmentation.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red algae reproduce through ****Fragmentation**.

 
 
• **Red algae** is the numerous algae that **constitute the phylum Rhodophyta. **
 
• It contains a **red pigment** in addition to chlorophyll.
 
• The group includes **carrageen, dulse, and laver also called red seaweed.**
 
• It reproduces sexually as well as asexually.
 
• Asexual reproduction can occur through the production of spores and by vegetative means.
 
• It includes** fragmentation, cell division or propagules production.**
 
• **Fragmentation** is a method where **one fragment from an organism's body is broken due to external physical causes.**
 
• **Each fragment then grows into different individuals.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fission**

 
 
• **​**The type of asexual reproduction in which a **microorganism splits in two equal halves is called as binary fission.**
 
• **Binary fission occurs in Amoeba.**
 
• The cells which split during binary fission have the potential to grow to the size of the original one.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• ​**Spore formation **is a method of** asexual reproduction.**
 
• Plants like** ferns, moss, and fungi **reproduce by this method.
 
• **Spores are unicellular reproductive bodies** present in sacs called **sporangia.**
 
• When spores mature sporangia burst and spores are carried to a different location by air, wind, and water.
 
 
 
• **Cutting**
 
 
• **Cutting** is a type of asexual reproduction.
 
• **​**A cutting is a **vegetative plant part.**
 
• It is severed from the parent plant in order to regenerate itself, thereby forming a whole new plant.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of large, brown seaweed that grows in shallow, nutrient-rich salt water near coastal fronts around the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelp.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelp**

 
 
• **​Kelp are large brown algae** that **live in cool, relatively shallow waters** close to the shore.
 
• They grow in dense groupings much like a forest on land.
 
• These underwater towers of kelp **provide food and shelter for thousands of marine species.**
 
• Kelp can **grow to be one hundred feet tall.**
 
• They are** food for abalones such as the California Red Abalone.**
 
• Kelp forests **make tons of oxygen for nearby waters.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seagrass**

 
 
• **​Seagrasses are underwater plants** that evolved from land plants.
 
• They are** like terrestrial plants in that they have leaves, flowers, seeds, and roots.**
 
• They are a very** important food source and habitat for wildlife.**
 
• They have been called **“the lungs of the sea”** because they release oxygen into the water through the process of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Corals**
 
 
• **​Corals are small marine animals. **
 
• The “hard” type of coral grows with the help of algae, which gives it color and nutrients that help it form a sturdy, stony skeleton.
 
• Reefs, which form through the accumulation of hard coral are a vital ecosystem.
 
• It **supports an estimated 25% of ocean species.**

questions.question: When the government resorts to borrowing only to clear the backlog of interest payments, it is referred to as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero primary deficit.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zero primary deficit**

 
 
• **​Zero primary deficit means the government resorts to borrowing only to clear the existing backlog of interest payments.**
 
• It is not adding to the existing loans for any purpose other than meeting its existing obligations of interest payment.
 
• It is a sign of fiscal discipline or fiscal responsibility on the part of the government.
 
• A high primary deficit, on the other hand, reflects the fiscal irresponsibility of the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zero revenue deficit **

 
 
• **The shortfall of total revenue receipts compared to total revenue expenditure is defined as a revenue deficit.**
 
• It is related to only revenue expenditure and revenue receipts of the government.
 
• It signifies that the government’s own earnings are insufficient to meet the normal functioning of government departments.
 
• Revenue deficit** results in borrowing.**
 
 
 
• **Zero fiscal deficit**
 
 
• **A fiscal deficit is estimated as the difference between total expenditure and total receipts.**
 
• The Gross fiscal deficit is also estimated as the sum total of borrowing from RBI.
 
• **​**The fiscal deficit in the economy will be zero if there is no provision for borrowings in the budget.
 
 
 
• **Excess budget deficit**
 
 
• **A budget deficit occurs when expenses exceed revenue.**
 
• The government generally uses the term budget deficit when referring to spending rather than businesses or individuals. 
 
• Countries can counter budget deficits by raising taxes and cutting spending.

questions.question: The term 'header' is associated to which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Football.**__

__
 
• **A header is a technique that is used in association football to control the ball using the head to pass, shoot or clear.**
 
• This can be **done by standing, jumping, or diving position.**
 
• The header is a **common technique **and is used by players in almost every match.
 
• A** forward uses a header to score a goal.**
 
• A **defender uses a header to prevent the scoring of a goa**l by the opponent. 
 
• A header is the only option when the ball is in the air, because of the rule that a player can’t make contact with the ball using their hands.
 
• Most header goals are scored as a result of a cross or a corner. 
 
• **Tim Cahill, Marco van Basten, and Cristiano Ronaldo **are some players who are notable for their quality headers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The aim of football is to score more goals than the opponent in a **90-minute playing time frame.**
 
• The match is split up into** two halves of 45 minutes.**
 
• After the first 45 minutes, players will take a **15-minute rest period called half time.**
 
• The second 45 minutes will resume.
 
• **Two teams of eleven players** each compete to get the ball into the other team's goal.
 
• The team that has scored more goals at the end of the game is the winner.
 
• If both teams have scored an equal number of goals then the game is a draw.

questions.question: Identify the group of the periodic table to which cobalt belongs
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 9.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Group 9**

 
 
• **​**Group 9 is a **group of chemical elements** in the periodic table.
 
• Members are **cobalt, rhodium, iridium and meitnerium.**
 
• These are all** transition metals in the d-block.**
 
• All the elements in Period 9 are **speculative; except for Ust and Usq.**
 
• **Cobalt was first discovered in 1735 by George Brandt **in Stockholm Sweden.
 
• It is used in many places today, such as **magnets materials, paint pigments, glasses, and even cancer therapy.**
 
• The word cobalt is from the German word kobold, which means "goblin" or "evil spirit".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group 6**

 
 
• **​**This period contains the** lanthanides, also known as the rare earths.**
 
• Many lanthanides are known for **their magnetic properties, such as neodymium.**
 
• Many group 6 transition metals are very **valuable, such as gold.**
 
• However group 6 other metals are incredibly toxic, such as thallium.
 
 
 
• **Group 5**
 
 
• Group 5A (or VA) of the periodic table are **the pnictogens.**
 
• The nonmetals **nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P), the metalloids arsenic (As) and antimony (Sb), and the metal bismuth (Bi).**
 
• Compounds made from elements in Group 5 of the periodic table can help athletes increase endurance and build muscle.
 
• They're involved in making** chemical weapons used in war.**
 
 
 
• **Group 7**
 
 
• The elements in group 7 are d block elements.
 
• The three common Group 7 elements are They are manganese (Mn), technetium (Tc), rhenium (Re), and bohrium (Bh)
 
• ​Group 7 elements are also called transition metals as they come under d block elements.

questions.question: Which of the following mountains is formed as a result of the compression of tectonic plates, leading to the formation of large fold-like structures on the Earth's crust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ural mountain in Russia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Urals are among **the world's oldest extant mountain ranges.**
 
• For its age of 250 to 300 million years, the elevation of the mountains is unusually high.
 
• They are** formed as a result of the compression of tectonic plates, leading to the formation of large fold-like structures on the Earth's crust.**
 
• They formed during the** Uralian orogeny.**
 
• The formation occurred due to the collision of the eastern edge of the supercontinent Laurasia with the young and rheologically weak continent of **Kazakhstania. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• They have** rich resources**, including **metal ores, coal, and precious and semi-precious stones**.
 
• It contains more than **1,000 different types of valuable minerals.**
 
• Since the 18th century, the mountains have contributed significantly to the mineral sector of the Russian economy.
 
• The region is one of the** largest producers of metallurgy** and** heavy industry production in the country.**
 
• The Urals are divided, from north to south, into** the Polar (or Arctic), Nether-Polar (or Sub-Arctic), Northern, Central and Southern parts.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “Supreme Court to be a court of record”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 129.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Article 129

 
 
• ​Article 129 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
 
• The Supreme Court shall have all the powers of such a court, including the power to punish for contempt of itself. 
 
• Court of Record is defined as
 
 
• a court whereof the acts and judicial proceedings are enrolled for a perpetual memorial and testimony
 
• which has the power to fine and imprison for contempt of its authority 
 
 
 
• Contempt of court signifies not only a willful disregard or disobedience of its orders, but such conduct as tends to bring the authority of the court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Article 135 was included in the Constitution to enable the Supreme Court to exercise jurisdiction in cases.
 
• Article 126 Appointment of acting Chief Justice – Constitution Of India
 
 
• When the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by such one of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.
 
 
 
• The purpose behind Article 131 of the Indian Constitution is to uphold the spirit of cooperative federalism between the organs of the government.
 
• Under this Article, the Supreme Court has the original jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the matters of dispute between the states or between the center and state.

questions.question: How is tuberculosis spread in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct option is__** Droplet Infection.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB)** is an infectious disease usually caused by the** Bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis**.
 
• **Robert Koch** received **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1905** for the discover of the bacteria causing TB.
 
• The only available vaccine as of 2021 is** Bacillus Calmette-Guérin** commonly known as BCG.
 
• Intradermal** MVA85A** vaccine in addition to BCG injection is not effective in preventing tuberculosis.
 
• **The World Health Organization (WHO)** declared TB a **"global health emergency"** in **1993**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• TB is an airborne disease (diseases that spread through air). Another example of such disease is Covid-19.
 
• In 2020, an estimated 10 million people developed active TB, resulting in 1.5 million deaths, making TB the** second leading cause of death** from an infectious disease after COVID-19.
 
• More than 50% of cases being diagnosed in seven countries:
 
 
• **India (27%)**
 
• **China (9%)**
 
• **Indonesia (8%)**
 
• **Philippines (6%)**
 
• **Pakistan (6%)**
 
• **Nigeria (4%)**
 
• **Bangladesh (4%) **
 
 
 
• **Dr. Harshvardhan, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare **launched the new **TB Harega Desh Jeetega Campaign**.

questions.question: What is the name of the autobiography written by Mr Abhinav Bindra, the Olympic medallist from India?

• **Abhinav Apjit Bindra** is an **Indian Olympic gold medallist**, retired sports shooter, and businessman.
 
• He is the first Indian to win an Individual Olympic Gold Medal in the 2008 Summer Olympics.
 
• He is the recipient of the Padma Bhushan from the Government of India and is one of the top influencers of sports policy in the country.
 
• In 2018, Abhinav was bestowed with the prestigious Blue Cross, the ISSF's highest honor.

• On September 5, 2016, he announced his retirement.

questions.question: WINTER Olympics 2026 will be hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct option is__** Italy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first Winter Olympic Games, the** 1924 Winter Olympics**, were held in** Chamonix, France**.
 
• The Games were held every four years from 1924 to 1936, interrupted in 1940 and 1944 by World War II, and resumed in 1948.
 
• Five main sports** Bobsleigh, Curling, Ice Hockey, Nordic skiing, and Skating** are played in Winter Olympics.
 
• **The 2026 Winter Olympics will be hosted by Italy.**
 
• The Winter Olympic Games have been hosted on three continents by thirteen countries.
 
• The **USA** has hosted the Winter Olympics four times in **1932, 1960, 1980, and 2002**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baron Pierre de Coubertin** founded the** International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894.**
 
• The first modern Summer Olympic Games were held in** Athens, Greece in 1896**.
 
• The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD.
 
• Japan was the host nation of the 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo, 
 
• The Summer Olympics 2024 is organized in Paris.
 
• The last Summer Olympics was organized in Tokyo, Japan.
 
• Organizers of the 2024 Paris Olympics unveiled “Games Wide Open” as their official slogan on 25 July 2022.
 
• Having previously hosted in 1900 and 1924, Paris will be hosting the Summer Olympics third time in 2024.
 
• The 2024 Summer Olympics are scheduled to take place from July 26 to August 11, 2024.
 
• Athletes will compete in a total of 329 events in 32 sports.
 
• **Norway** was at the top in the medal tally in the 2022 Winter Olympics.

questions.question: The Ganga plain extend between which two rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghaggar and Teesta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ganga Plain which lies between **Ghaggar and Teesta** rivers is characterized by quaternary alluvia with combinations of clay, silt, sand, and gravel.
 
• The states,** of Haryana, Delhi, UP, Bihar, part of Jharkhand, and West Bengal** lie in the Ganga plains.
 
• This plain covers most of the part of Northern Plains.
 
• The Ganga plain stretches from** Delhi to Kolkata** covering about** 3.7 lakh sq km**.
 
• The peninsular rivers like** Ken, Chambal, Betwa, Son,** etc. joining the Ganga river system contributed to the formation of this plain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India is divided into six main parts that are The Great Mountain Range, Northern Plains, Desert Region, Peninsular Plateaus, Coastal Plains, and Island group. 
 
• The total geographical area of India is** 3.28 million square km**.
 
• The longest river in India is** Ganga** which is** 2,525 km** long.
 
• India has the** 18th largest Exclusive Economic Zone** of** 2,305,143 km2 (890,021 sq mi)**.
 
• India has **7,516 km** long coastline. Canada has the longest coastline in the world.
